Friction is a force that happens when two surfaces rub together. It's the force that slows objects down!

Ang friction ay isang puwersa na nangyayari kapag nagkiskisan ang dalawang ibabaw. Ito ang nagpapabagal sa mga bagay!

Unsa ang friction?

Ang friction usa ka kusog nga mahitabo kon maggidlanay ang duha ka ibabaw. Kini ang makapahinay sa mga butang!

How does a refrigerator keep your food cold?

A refrigerator is a machine that pulls heat out from inside and releases it outside, keeping the inside cold!
copy.tl:
Paano pinapanatiling malamig ng refrigerator ang pagkain?

Ang refrigerator ay isang makina na inaalis ang init mula sa loob at inilalabas ito sa labas, kaya nananatiling malamig!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpabugnaw sa pridyider sa pagkaon?

Ang pridyider usa ka makina nga magkuha sa init gikan sa sulod ug ipagawas kini sa gawas, busa magpabiling bugnaw ang sulod!

copy.tl: Kapag nilagyan ng mainit na pagkain ang ref, mas marami itong init na kailangang ilipat palabas!
copy.bis: Kon butangan og mainit nga pagkaon ang ref, mas daghan ang kainit nga kinahanglan ipagawas niini!

How far can a frog jump compared to its size?

Much farther than its own body length! Even though frogs are small, they can cover a surprisingly long distance in a single jump.
copy.tl:
Gaano kalayo ang kayang lukso ng palaka kumpara sa laki niya?

Mas malayo pa kaysa sa haba ng sarili niyang katawan! Kahit maliit lang ang palaka, sobrang layo ng naaabot niya sa isang lukso.
copy.bis:
Unsa kalayo ang maambakan sa baki kumpara sa iyang gidak-on?

Mas layo pa kaysa sa gitas-on sa iyang kaugalingong lawas! Bisan gamay ra ang baki, layo kaayo ang maabot niini sa usa ka lukso.

copy.en: Male frogs use vocal sacs, which are pouches of loose skin under their mouths, to amplify their calls and reach females farther away!
copy.tl: Gumagamit ang mga lalaking palaka ng vocal sac—mga maluwag na balat sa ilalim ng bibig—para palakihin ang tawag at maabot ang malalayong babae!
copy.bis: Naggamit ang mga lalaking palaka og vocal sac—mga baldus nga panit sa ilalim sa baba—sa pagpalaka sa ilang tawag aron maabot ang layo nga mga babaye!

copy.en: Farmers cover vegetables with plastic or cloth at night to protect them! This traps a little heat from the ground, keeping the leaves warm enough so they don't freeze.
copy.tl: Tinatakpan ng mga magsasaka ang gulay ng plastik o tela sa gabi para protektahan sila! Nakukulong nito ang konting init mula sa lupa para hindi magyelo ang mga dahon.
copy.bis: Gitabonan sa mag-uuma ang mga utanon og plastik o tela sa gabii aron protektahan sila! Makapugong kini sa gamayng init gikan sa yuta aron dili mo-yelo ang mga dahon.

copy.en:
Why can thawed food spoil?

When frozen food thaws and warms up again, it can spoil because the bacteria become active again!
copy.tl:
Bakit mapapanis ang natunaw na pagkain?

Kapag natunaw at uminit muli ang frozen na pagkain, maaari na itong mapanis dahil nabubuhay muli ang bakterya!
copy.bis:
Nganong mapanis ang natunaw nga pagkaon?

Kon matunaw ug moinit pag-usab ang frozen nga pagkaon, mahimo kining mapanis tungod kay ang bakterya mabuhi pag-usab!

copy.en:
How do large fruit bats find food?

Unlike many other bats, large fruit bats use their sharp eyesight and sense of smell to find food, not echolocation.
copy.tl:
Paano naghahanap ng pagkain ang malaking paniki?

Hindi tulad ng ibang paniki, ang malalaking paniki na kumakain ng prutas ay gumagamit ng matalas na mata at pang-amoy para makahanap ng pagkain.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpangita og pagkaon sa dagkong kabog?

Dili sama sa ubang kabog, ang dagkong kabog nga mokaon og prutas mogamit sa ilang isog nga mata ug pagpaninghot aron makakaplag og pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fruit bats rely on their big eyes and strong sense of smell instead of echolocation to find fruit.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food

copy.en:
Do fruit bats use echolocation to find fruit?

Surprise — most don't! Fruit bats rely on their big eyes and strong sense of smell instead of echolocation to find fruit.
copy.tl:
Gumagamit ba ng echolocation ang fruit bat?

Nakakagulat — hindi pala! Karamihan ng fruit bat ay umaasa sa malalaki nilang mata at matalas na pang-amoy, hindi sa echolocation, para makahanap ng prutas.
copy.bis:
Naggamit ba og echolocation ang fruit bat?

Katingala — dili diay! Kasagaran sa fruit bat nagsalig sa ilang dagkong mata ug hait nga panimho, dili sa echolocation, aron makakita og prutas.

copy.bis: Mamulak una ang santol, atis, ug guyabano sa dili pa mahimong prutas ang ilang mga bulak.

The Fujita scale rates a tornado's strength based on the damage it causes!

copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagsukod sa kusog sa usa ka tornado?

Ang Fujita scale nagsukod sa kusog sa tornado base sa kadaot nga gipahinabo niini!

copy.bis: Ang uhong ganahan motubo sa mabasa ug ngitngit nga mga dapit sama sa nadunot nga kahoy o basa nga yuta.

copy.en:
Why do hyphae need a damp place?

Hyphae need a damp, moist place because they soak up food dissolved in water — too dry, and the fungus stops growing, which is why mold spreads faster when it's warm and wet.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng hyphae ng basang lugar?

Kailangan ng hyphae ng basa o mahalumigmig na lugar dahil sinisipsip nila ang pagkaing natunaw sa tubig — kapag masyadong tuyo, tumitigil ang paglaki ng fungi, kaya mas mabilis kumalat ang amag kapag mainit at basa.
copy.bis:
Ngano nagkinahanglan og basa nga dapit ang hyphae?

Nanginahanglan ang hyphae og basa o umog nga dapit kay mosuyop sila og pagkaon nga natunaw sa tubig — kon uga kaayo, muhunong ang pagtubo sa fungi, mao nga mas paspas mokaylap ang agup-op kon init ug basa.

copy.en: Fungi can reproduce without a mate — through spores or budding — or by joining two special spores together; that sexual way creates even more genetic diversity in fungus populations.
copy.tl: Ang mga fungi ay maaaring magparami nang wala pang kapareha — sa pamamagitan ng spore o budding — o sa pagsasanib ng dalawang espesyal na spore; ang paraang ito ay nagbibigay ng mas maraming genetic diversity sa mga fungi.
copy.bis: Ang mga fungi mahimong magparami nga wala pay padoyupdoyop — pinaagi sa spore o budding — o sa paghiusa sa duha ka espesyal nga spore; kini nga paagi maghatag og mas daghang genetic diversity sa mga fungi.

copy.en:
How do feathers and fur keep animals warm?

Feathers and fur trap a layer of air close to the body! This cozy air pocket stops body heat from escaping into the cold surroundings.
copy.tl:
Paano pinapanatiling mainit ng balahibo at buhok ang mga hayop?

Ang balahibo at buhok ay nagtatago ng layer ng hangin malapit sa katawan! Ang nakakulong na hangin ay pumipigil sa init ng katawan na tumakas sa malamig na paligid.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpainit sa mga balahibo ug buhok sa mga hayop?

Ang mga balahibo ug buhok nagtatago og layer sa hangin duol sa lawas! Kining nakulong nga hangin nagpugong sa init sa lawas nga mokalagiw sa bugnaw nga palibot.

copy.tl: Gumagamit ang circuit breaker ng switch at maliit na electromagnet! Kapag lumakas ang kuryente, hinihila ng magnet ang switch para putulin ang kuryente nang walang natutunaw.
copy.bis: Ang circuit breaker naggamit og switch ug gamay nga electromagnet! Kung mokusog ang kuryente, birahon sa magnet ang switch aron putlon ang kuryente nga walay matunaw.

When two bare wires touch, a huge current rushes through a short path! The fuse or breaker senses this fast and immediately cuts the flow.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa short circuit?

Kapag nagdikit ang dalawang hubad na wire, biglang dumadaloy ang napakalaking kuryente! Mabilis itong namamansin ng fuse o breaker at agad pinuputol.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa short circuit?

Kung magdikit ang duha ka hubo nga wire, kalit nga modagan ang dako kaayo nga kuryente! Paspas kini mamatikdan sa fuse o breaker ug dihadiha moputol.

copy.en:
Why do stars like the Sun shine and give off heat?

Nuclear fusion inside a star releases great amounts of energy over millions of years! This is why stars like the Sun shine and give off heat.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagliliwanag at umiinit ang mga bituin tulad ng Araw?

Ang nuclear fusion sa loob ng bituin ay naglalabas ng napakalaking enerhiya sa loob ng milyon-milyong taon! Kaya nagliliwanag at umiinit ang mga bituin tulad ng Araw.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagdan-ag ug nagpainit ang mga bituon sama sa Adlaw?

Ang nuclear fusion sulod sa bituon nagpagawas og dako kaayong enerhiya sulod sa minilyon ka tuig! Mao kini ang hinungdan nganong nagdan-ag ug nagpainit ang mga bituon sama sa Adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Aerogel is a super lightweight synthetic solid! It's made by swapping the liquid in a gel with gas, making it 99 percent air.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions solid, liquid, and gas as words but does not teach that matter exists in three states. It is a specific fact about aerogel, not instruction on the three states of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Aerogel is a super lightweight synthetic solid! It's made by swapping the liquid in a gel with gas, making it 99 percent air.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe shape and volume properties of solids, liquids, or gases. It only notes aerogel is a solid and 99% air, which does not directly support the competency's focus on definite/indefinite shape and volume.

copy.en: Aerogel is a super lightweight synthetic solid! It's made by swapping the liquid in a gel with gas, making it 99 percent air.
copy.tl: Ang aerogel ay isang napakagaan na synthetic solid material! Ginawa ito sa pamamagitan ng pagpapalit ng likido sa gel ng gas, kaya 99 porsyento itong hangin.
copy.bis: Ang aerogel usa ka sobra ka gaan nga synthetic solid material! Gihimo kini pinaagi sa pag-ilisan sa likido sa gel og gas, mao nga 99 porsyento kini hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Agusan River flows northward into Butuan Bay, draining rainwater from the Caraga region back into the Bohol Sea!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a local river and bay, which are examples of bodies of water, but it does not describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment. The content is limited to the river's flow and drainage, not the required influence on environmental components.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Agusan River flows northward into Butuan Bay, draining rainwater from the Caraga region back into the Bohol Sea!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water and rain, which are non-living things, but it does not involve guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around school. It is a factual statement about a specific river, not an activity-based description of non-living things in the school environment.

copy.en: The Agusan River flows northward into Butuan Bay, draining rainwater from the Caraga region back into the Bohol Sea!
copy.tl: Ang Ilog Agusan ay dumadaloy pa-hilaga papunta sa Butuan Bay, nagdadala ng tubig-ulan mula sa Caraga region pabalik sa Bohol Sea!
copy.bis: Ang Suba sa Agusan nagdagan pa-norte paingon sa Butuan Bay, nagdala sa tubig-ulan gikan sa Caraga region pabalik sa Bohol Sea!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air is a mixture of 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes air as a mixture of nitrogen and oxygen only, omitting carbon dioxide and water vapor, which are required components in the competency. It does not directly support the full description of air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor.

copy.en: Air is a mixture of 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen, meaning it contains nearly four times more nitrogen than oxygen!
copy.tl: Ang hangin ay halo ng 78 percent nitrogen at 21 percent oxygen, kaya halos apat na beses mas maraming nitrogen kaysa oxygen!
copy.bis: Ang hangin kay sagol nga 78 percent nitrogen ug 21 percent oxygen, mao nga hapit upat ka beses mas daghan ang nitrogen kaysa oxygen!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's atmosphere contains about 21% oxygen gas
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions only oxygen as a component of air and does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It gives a percentage for oxygen but does not teach the mixture composition required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: which is necessary for combustion and rusting
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that oxygen is necessary for combustion and rusting, which touches on a chemical property, but it does not describe chemical properties of materials such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. The support is too indirect for this competency.

copy.en:
What gas in our air helps things burn and rust?

Earth's atmosphere contains about 21% oxygen gas, which is necessary for combustion and rusting!
copy.tl:
Anong gas sa ating hangin ang nakakatulong sa pagsusunog at pagkalawang?

Ang atmospera ng Earth ay may halos 21% oxygen gas, na kailangan para sa combustion at pagkalawang!
copy.bis:
Unhang gas sa atong hangin ang makatabang sa pagsunog ug pagkalawang?

Ang atmospera sa Yuta adunay mga 21% oxygen gas, nga importante para sa combustion ug pagkalawang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This shape reduces air friction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions reducing air friction via a streamlined shape, which touches on one way to reduce friction, but it does not demonstrate how friction produces heat nor investigate ways of reducing/increasing friction. It is a single factual example without the required demonstration or investigation.

copy.en: The MRT-3 train in Manila has a streamlined, pointed nose! This shape reduces air friction, helping it move faster and use less energy.
copy.tl: Ang MRT-3 train sa Manila ay may makinis at matulis na ilong! Binabawasan nito ang air friction, kaya mas mabilis itong gumalaw at mas kaunti ang enerhiyang ginagamit.
copy.bis: Ang MRT-3 train sa Manila adunay streamlined ug pointed nga nose! Nagpakunhod kini sa air friction, mao nga mas paspas siya mo-move ug gamay ra ang energy nga gigamit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This air resistance limits their maximum terminal velocity to about 195 kilometers per hour.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions terminal velocity, which implies balanced forces, but it does not identify or describe balanced/unbalanced forces or the everyday situation in the way the competency requires. It is related vocabulary without direct instructional support.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This air resistance limits their maximum terminal velocity to about 195 kilometers per hour.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces cause objects to accelerate, and that acceleration of an object is its rate of change of velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses terminal velocity but does not explain that forces cause acceleration or that acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. It does not directly support the competency's core concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A skydiver falling in a belly-to-earth position experiences air resistance!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air resistance but does not involve planning or carrying out an investigation about different surfaces and frictional forces. It is only related to the topic of friction/air resistance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A skydiver falling in a belly-to-earth position experiences air resistance!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a falling skydiver and air resistance, but it does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object in a way that teaches the competency. Gravity is implied but not explained.

copy.en: A skydiver falling in a belly-to-earth position experiences air resistance! This air resistance limits their maximum terminal velocity to about 195 kilometers per hour.
copy.tl: Ang skydiver na naka-belly-to-earth position ay nakararanas ng air resistance! Ang air resistance na ito ang naglilimita sa kanyang terminal velocity sa halos 195 kilometers per hour.
copy.bis: Ang skydiver nga naka-belly-to-earth position makasinati ug air resistance! Kining air resistance ang mo-limit sa iyang terminal velocity sa mga 195 kilometro kada oras.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As altitude increases on Mount Pulag, atmospheric pressure decreases! This causes air temperature to drop, creating a colder climate.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure and air temperature, which are named weather characteristics, but it does not teach students to identify these as basic characteristics used to describe weather. Instead, it explains how altitude affects these variables. The focus is on altitude–climate relationships, not on identifying weather descriptors.

copy.en: As altitude increases on Mount Pulag, atmospheric pressure decreases! This causes air temperature to drop, creating a colder climate.
copy.tl: Habang tumataas ang altitude sa Mount Pulag, bumababa ang atmospheric pressure! Kaya lumalamig ang air temperature at nagiging colder ang climate.
copy.bis: Samtang mosaka ang altitude sa Mount Pulag, mo-ubos ang atmospheric pressure! Mao nga mobugnaw ang air temperature ug mag-himo og colder climate.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The amihan wind brings cool, dry weather to the Philippines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the weather effect of the Amihan (northeast monsoon). It does not explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of monsoons, land/sea breezes, or the ITCZ, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cool, dry weather
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a weather condition (cool, dry) but does not identify or describe basic weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, or cloud cover. It only gives a general description of the monsoon's effect.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: during the first few months of the year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to a seasonal weather pattern (Amihan) but does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities appropriate for each season. It only states one weather condition for part of the year.

copy.en:
What weather does the amihan wind bring?

The amihan wind brings cool, dry weather to the Philippines during the first few months of the year!
copy.tl:
Anong panahon ang dala ng amihan?

Ang amihan na hangin ay nagdadala ng malamig at tuyong panahon sa Pilipinas sa unang ilang buwan ng taon!
copy.bis:
Unsay panahon nga dala sa amihan?

Ang amihan nga hangin nagdala og bugnaw ug uga nga panahon sa Pilipinas sa unang mga bulan sa tuig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Mexican axolotl can completely regrow its lost limbs, spinal cord, heart, and even parts of its brain.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an animal's ability to regrow body parts, which is an organism-level example of growth and repair. However, it does not mention cells, mitosis, meiosis, or cell division, so it does not directly support the competency's focus on recognizing the two types of cell division and describing mitosis as cell division for growth and repair.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Mexican axolotl can completely regrow its lost limbs, spinal cord, heart, and even parts of its brain.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a remarkable animal ability (regeneration) but does not describe how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it provide an example of mimicry, camouflage, or other adaptive change. Regeneration is not presented as an environmental adaptation, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Which animal can regrow parts of its brain?

The Mexican axolotl can completely regrow its lost limbs, spinal cord, heart, and even parts of its brain.
copy.tl:
Anong hayop ang kayang magpatubo muli ng bahagi ng utak?

Ang Mexican axolotl ay kayang buuin muli nang lubusan ang nawalang mga paa, spinal cord, puso, at kahit bahagi ng utak.
copy.bis:
Unsang hayop ang makapatubo pag-usab og bahin sa utok?

Ang Mexican axolotl makapahiuli og hingpit sa nawala nga mga bukton, spinal cord, kasingkasing, ug bisan mga bahin sa utok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A blue whale's heart beats only about 10 times a minute when diving, but a mouse's tiny heart races at 500-600 beats a minute
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Comparing heartbeat rates is trivia, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en:
Whose heart beats faster — whale or mouse?

A blue whale's heart beats only about 10 times a minute when diving, but a mouse's tiny heart races at 500-600 beats a minute!
copy.tl:
Sino ang mas mabilis magpintig ang puso — balyena o daga?

Ang puso ng blue whale ay tumitibok lang ng mga 10 beses bawat minuto kapag sumisisid, pero ang puso ng daga ay umaabot ng 500-600 beses bawat minuto!
copy.bis:
Kinsa'y mas paspas mo-beat ang kasingkasing — balyena o ilaga?

Ang kasingkasing sa blue whale mo-beat lang og mga 10 ka beses matag minuto kung naglunod, apan ang kasingkasing sa ilaga mo-beat og 500-600 ka beses matag minuto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sugar molecules are completely dissolved in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a solution (sugar in water) but does not identify which component is the solute and which is the solvent, nor explain their roles. It only states that sugar is dissolved in water, which is background knowledge rather than direct instruction for identifying solute/solvent roles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a sweet aqueous solution where sugar molecules are completely dissolved in water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an aqueous solution as an example of a uniform mixture, but it does not describe the characteristics of uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, nor contrast solutions with suspensions. It only labels nectar as a solution, providing no direct support for describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures.

copy.en:
What's inside a sampaguita flower's nectar?

It's a sweet aqueous solution where sugar molecules are completely dissolved in water!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nasa nektar ng bulaklak na sampaguita?

Ito ay isang matamis na aqueous solution kung saan ang sugar molecules ay ganap na natutunaw sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang sulod sa nektar sa bulak nga sampaguita?

Kini usa ka tam-is nga aqueous solution diin ang sugar molecules hingpit nga natunaw sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If all water vapor in Earth's atmosphere rained down at once, it would cover the whole globe in just 2.5 centimeters of water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions water vapor as a component of air, but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It provides a trivia fact about the total amount of water vapor, not the composition of air.

copy.en: If all water vapor in Earth's atmosphere rained down at once, it would cover the whole globe in just 2.5 centimeters of water!
copy.tl: Kung lahat ng water vapor sa Earth's atmosphere ay biglang uulanin, mababasa lang ang buong mundo ng 2.5 sentimetro na tubig!
copy.bis: Kung ang tanang water vapor sa atmospera sa Yuta muulan sa usa ka higayon, matabunan lang ang kalibutan og 2.5 sentimetro nga tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Baking soda is a base that chemically reacts with acidic smell molecules
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies baking soda as a base found at home, but the competency requires identifying solutions that react with litmus indicator as acids, bases, and salts. No litmus indicator or solution context is present, so the card only shares vocabulary about bases without directly supporting the litmus-based identification skill.

copy.en: Baking soda is a base that chemically reacts with acidic smell molecules to neutralize sour odors inside your refrigerator!
copy.tl: Ang baking soda ay isang base na chemically nag-rereact sa acidic smell molecules para i-neutralize ang maasim na amoy sa loob ng refrigerator!
copy.bis: Ang baking soda usa ka base nga chemically mo-react sa acidic smell molecules aron i-neutralize ang aslum nga baho sulod sa ref!
